name: One Pure Two-Apex Wing Resolves the Sharp, Uncounted, and Two-Unit Rows
statement: Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ of order at most nine. If one wing has the pure $\eta=2$ two-apex form and the opposite wing is sharp, has the uncounted $\eta=1$ one-unit form, or has any feasible two-unit profile, then their acquired supports contain three pairwise disjoint direction pairs.
proof: An exact-profile audit constructs all two-vertex completions of the pure $P_7$ spine, retains 158 embedded ample overlaps, rediscovers each pure decomposition, and recognizes the opposite profiles from their structural normal forms and the exact excess identity. Every one of 2268 comparisons ends in a repeated acquired terminal pair, a terminal matching of order three, a passive-distance-two corner, a forced-owner conflict, a repeated acquired collar, or a matching after collars are added. Repetitions contradict shadow intersection, distant corners contradict radius-one shielding, and owner conflicts force a word into $B$ or both disjoint exclusive sets. The two matching outcomes give the conclusion directly.
comments: With marker multiplicities retained, the audit classifies sharp comparisons as 16 repeated-terminal and 3 terminal-matching outcomes; eta-one comparisons as 172 repeated-terminal, 42 terminal-matching, and 2 distant-corner outcomes; and feasible two-unit comparisons as 1188 repeated-terminal, 592 terminal-matching, 118 distant-corner, 95 owner-conflict, 24 repeated-collar, and 16 collar-matching outcomes.
